questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Find the length of a side of a rhombus whose diagonals are 6 cm and 8 cm.
questions.ai_explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. Half-diagonals of 3 cm and 4 cm form the legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is a side of the rhombus. The side length is √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 cm.
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. Half-diagonals of 3 cm and 4 cm form the legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is a side of the rhombus. The side length is √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 cm.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: If cos θ = 12/13, find 1 + cot² θ.
questions.ai_explanation: Use sin² θ = 1 − cos² θ = 1 − 144/169 = 25/169. Therefore cot² θ = cos² θ/sin² θ = 144/25, and 1 + cot² θ = 169/25. Equivalently, 1 + cot² θ = 1/sin² θ. Squared values make the result independent of the sign of sin θ.
questions.explanation: Use sin² θ = 1 − cos² θ = 1 − 144/169 = 25/169. Therefore cot² θ = cos² θ/sin² θ = 144/25, and 1 + cot² θ = 169/25. Equivalently, 1 + cot² θ = 1/sin² θ. Squared values make the result independent of the sign of sin θ.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: In triangle XYZ shown, angle YXZ = 30°, angle XYZ = 105° and XY = 8 cm. Calculate YZ.
questions.ai_explanation: The angles in a triangle sum to 180°, so angle XZY = 180° − 30° − 105° = 45°. By the sine rule, YZ/sin 30° = 8/sin 45°. Therefore YZ = 8 × (1/2)/(√2/2) = 4√2 cm.
questions.image_alt: Triangle XYZ with XY labelled 8 cm, angle X labelled 30° and angle Y labelled 105°.
questions.explanation: The angles in a triangle sum to 180°, so angle XZY = 180° − 30° − 105° = 45°. By the sine rule, YZ/sin 30° = 8/sin 45°. Therefore YZ = 8 × (1/2)/(√2/2) = 4√2 cm.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Two distinct numbers are drawn at random without replacement from 1, 2, 3 and 4. What is the probability that their sum is even?
questions.ai_explanation: The six equally likely unordered pairs are {1,2}, {1,3}, {1,4}, {2,3}, {2,4} and {3,4}. Only {1,3} and {2,4} have even sums, so the probability is 2/6 = 1/3. An even sum requires two odd numbers or two even numbers.
questions.explanation: The six equally likely unordered pairs are {1,2}, {1,3}, {1,4}, {2,3}, {2,4} and {3,4}. Only {1,3} and {2,4} have even sums, so the probability is 2/6 = 1/3. An even sum requires two odd numbers or two even numbers.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: An integer is selected uniformly at random from 41 to 56 inclusive. What is the probability that it is a multiple of 9?
questions.ai_explanation: There are 56 − 41 + 1 = 16 integers in the inclusive range. The multiples of 9 are 45 and 54, so there are two favourable outcomes. The probability is 2/16 = 1/8.
questions.explanation: There are 56 − 41 + 1 = 16 integers in the inclusive range. The multiples of 9 are 45 and 54, so there are two favourable outcomes. The probability is 2/16 = 1/8.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: If w varies inversely as uv/(u + v), and w = 8 when u = 2 and v = 6, find the relationship between u, v and w.
questions.ai_explanation: Inverse variation gives w = k(u + v)/(uv). Substituting the given values, 8 = k(2 + 6)/(2 × 6), so k = 12. Therefore uvw = 12(u + v). The relation applies where u, v and u + v are nonzero.
questions.explanation: Inverse variation gives w = k(u + v)/(uv). Substituting the given values, 8 = k(2 + 6)/(2 × 6), so k = 12. Therefore uvw = 12(u + v). The relation applies where u, v and u + v are nonzero.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is a factor of rs + tr − pt − ps?
questions.ai_explanation: Group the terms: rs + tr − pt − ps = r(s + t) − p(t + s) = (r − p)(s + t). Therefore r − p is a factor.
questions.explanation: Group the terms: rs + tr − pt − ps = r(s + t) − p(t + s) = (r − p)(s + t). Therefore r − p is a factor.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Find the two values of y that satisfy the simultaneous equations 3x + y = 8 and x² + xy = 6.
questions.ai_explanation: From the first equation, y = 8 − 3x. Substitute into the second: x² + x(8 − 3x) = 6, so x² − 4x + 3 = 0. Factor to obtain (x − 1)(x − 3) = 0. When x = 1, y = 5; when x = 3, y = −1. Thus the two values of y are −1 and 5.
questions.explanation: From the first equation, y = 8 − 3x. Substitute into the second: x² + x(8 − 3x) = 6, so x² − 4x + 3 = 0. Factor to obtain (x − 1)(x − 3) = 0. When x = 1, y = 5; when x = 3, y = −1. Thus the two values of y are −1 and 5.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Find the range of x that satisfies x/2 + x/3 + x/4 < 1.
questions.ai_explanation: Use the common denominator 12: x/2 + x/3 + x/4 = (6x + 4x + 3x)/12 = 13x/12. Multiplying the inequality by the positive number 12/13 gives x < 12/13. The boundary value is excluded because the inequality is strict.
questions.explanation: Use the common denominator 12: x/2 + x/3 + x/4 = (6x + 4x + 3x)/12 = 13x/12. Multiplying the inequality by the positive number 12/13 gives x < 12/13. The boundary value is excluded because the inequality is strict.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Solve the equation (x − 2)(x − 3) = 12.
questions.ai_explanation: Expand and collect terms: x² − 5x + 6 = 12, so x² − 5x − 6 = 0. Factor to obtain (x − 6)(x + 1) = 0. Hence x = 6 or x = −1. Substituting either value into the original equation gives 12.
questions.explanation: Expand and collect terms: x² − 5x + 6 = 12, so x² − 5x − 6 = 0. Factor to obtain (x − 6)(x + 1) = 0. Hence x = 6 or x = −1. Substituting either value into the original equation gives 12.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Simplify (√(1 + x) + √x)/(√(1 + x) − √x).
questions.ai_explanation: Multiply the numerator and denominator by √(1 + x) + √x. The denominator becomes (1 + x) − x = 1. Expanding the numerator gives 1 + x + x + 2√(x(1 + x)) = 1 + 2x + 2√(x(1 + x)). For real square roots, x ≥ 0.
questions.explanation: Multiply the numerator and denominator by √(1 + x) + √x. The denominator becomes (1 + x) − x = 1. Expanding the numerator gives 1 + x + x + 2√(x(1 + x)) = 1 + 2x + 2√(x(1 + x)). For real square roots, x ≥ 0.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: What is the nth term of the progression 27, 9, 3, …?
questions.ai_explanation: This is a geometric progression with first term 27 and common ratio 9/27 = 1/3. Its nth term is ar^(n − 1), so the required term is 27(1/3)^(n − 1), for n = 1, 2, 3, …. It gives 27, 9 and 3 for the first three terms.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: The angles of a quadrilateral are (5x − 30)°, (4x + 60)°, (60 − x)° and (3x + 61)°. Which is the smallest angle?
questions.ai_explanation: The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to 360°. Thus 11x + 151 = 360, giving x = 19. The four angles are 65°, 136°, 41° and 118°. The smallest is 41°, represented by (60 − x)°.
questions.explanation: The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to 360°. Thus 11x + 151 = 360, giving x = 19. The four angles are 65°, 136°, 41° and 118°. The smallest is 41°, represented by (60 − x)°.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: The area of a square is 144 cm². Find the length of its diagonal.
questions.ai_explanation: The side length is √144 = 12 cm. A diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with both shorter sides equal to 12 cm. By Pythagoras, d² = 12² + 12² = 288, so d = 12√2 cm.
questions.explanation: The side length is √144 = 12 cm. A diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with both shorter sides equal to 12 cm. By Pythagoras, d² = 12² + 12² = 288, so d = 12√2 cm.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: One angle of a rhombus is 60°. The shorter diagonal is 8 cm. Find the length of the longer diagonal.
questions.ai_explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect its angles and meet at right angles. In the resulting 30°–60°–90° triangle, half of the shorter diagonal is 4 cm. The longer half-diagonal is 4√3 cm, so the full longer diagonal is 8√3 cm.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: From a point P outside a circle, PT is a tangent. Two secants pass through the circle in the orders P–M–N and P–Q–R. If PM = 5 cm, PN = 12 cm and PQ = 4.8 cm, find PR and PT respectively, to the nearest 0.1 cm.
questions.ai_explanation: For secants from the same external point, PM × PN = PQ × PR = PT². The common product is 5 × 12 = 60 cm². Hence PR = 60/4.8 = 12.5 cm and PT = √60 ≈ 7.7 cm.
questions.explanation: For secants from the same external point, PM × PN = PQ × PR = PT². The common product is 5 × 12 = 60 cm². Hence PR = 60/4.8 = 12.5 cm and PT = √60 ≈ 7.7 cm.

questions.question: Simplify cos²x(sec²x + sec²x tan²x).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: PQRS is a square of side 8 cm, with its vertices named in order. U lies on PQ, V on QR and W on RS. Given UQ = 4 cm, QV = 6 cm and RW = 2 cm, find the area of triangle UVW.

questions.question: Find the total surface area of a solid cylinder whose base radius is 4 cm and height is 5 cm.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: A family spends 3% of its income on electricity, 59% on food, 20% on transport, 11% on education and 7% on extended family. What angles represent education and food, respectively, in a pie chart?

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Fifty boxes, each containing 50 balls, were inspected. The numbers of defective balls per box were 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9, with corresponding numbers of boxes 2, 7, 17, 10, 8 and 6. Find the mean (to one decimal place) and median number of defective balls per box, respectively.
questions.ai_explanation: The frequencies total 50. The weighted total is 4×2 + 5×7 + 6×17 + 7×10 + 8×8 + 9×6 = 333, so the mean is 333/50 = 6.66, or 6.7 to one decimal place. There are 9 values below 6 and 26 values at or below 6. Both the 25th and 26th values are 6, so the median is 6.
questions.explanation: The frequencies total 50. The weighted total is 4×2 + 5×7 + 6×17 + 7×10 + 8×8 + 9×6 = 333, so the mean is 333/50 = 6.66, or 6.7 to one decimal place. There are 9 values below 6 and 26 values at or below 6. Both the 25th and 26th values are 6, so the median is 6.

questions.question: Solve the equation y − 11√y + 24 = 0.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: For real numbers m and n, the binary operation * is defined by m*n = mn + m + n. Find its identity element.
questions.ai_explanation: An identity e must satisfy m*e = m for every m. Thus me + m + e = m, so e(m + 1) = 0 for every m. Taking m = 0 gives e = 0. Substitution confirms m*0 = m and 0*m = m.
questions.explanation: An identity e must satisfy m*e = m for every m. Thus me + m + e = m, so e(m + 1) = 0 for every m. Taking m = 0 gives e = 0. Substitution confirms m*0 = m and 0*m = m.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: P and R are the endpoints of a diameter of a circle, and Q is a point on the semicircle. PQ and QR are chords. S lies on PR, with QS perpendicular to PR. Which expression gives the length QS?
questions.ai_explanation: The angle PQR is 90° because PR is a diameter. The altitude QS divides the right triangle into two similar triangles, PQS and QRS. Their corresponding sides give PS/QS = QS/SR, so QS² = PS × SR. Taking the positive square root gives QS = √(PS × SR).
questions.explanation: The angle PQR is 90° because PR is a diameter. The altitude QS divides the right triangle into two similar triangles, PQS and QRS. Their corresponding sides give PS/QS = QS/SR, so QS² = PS × SR. Taking the positive square root gives QS = √(PS × SR).

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Towns P and Q both lie on latitude 60°N. Their longitudes are 20°E and 25°W respectively. Calculate the distance between them along this latitude, taking Earth’s radius as 6400 km.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Two perpendicular radii of a circle with centre O each have length 6 cm. A chord joins their endpoints. Find the area of the minor segment between this chord and the quarter-circle arc.
questions.ai_explanation: The perpendicular radii form a 90° sector. Its area is (90/360) × π × 6² = 9π cm². The right triangle formed by the radii has area ½ × 6 × 6 = 18 cm². The segment area is therefore 9π − 18 = 9(π − 2) cm².

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: The locus of a point which is equidistant from two given fixed points is the

options.A: perpendicular bisector of the straight line joining them
options.B: parallel line to the straight line joining them
options.C: transverse to the straight line joining them
options.D: angle bisector of 90° which the straight line joining them makes with the horizontal

questions.ai_explanation: Place the fixed points at (−a, 0) and (a, 0). Equal distances from (x, y) require (x + a)² + y² = (x − a)² + y². For two distinct fixed points, a ≠ 0, so x = 0. This is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining the points.
questions.explanation: Place the fixed points at (−a, 0) and (a, 0). Equal distances from (x, y) require (x + a)² + y² = (x − a)² + y². For two distinct fixed points, a ≠ 0, so x = 0. This is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining the points.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: Find the equation of the line through (5, 7) parallel to the line 7x + 5y = 12.
questions.ai_explanation: A parallel line has the same coefficients of x and y, so write it as 7x + 5y = c. Substituting (5, 7) gives c = 7×5 + 5×7 = 70. Hence the required equation is 7x + 5y = 70.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Three forces act at O in equilibrium. P₃ points horizontally left; P₁ points right at an acute angle θ₁ above the horizontal; P₂ points right at an acute angle θ₂ below the horizontal. Which relations must hold in general? I. P₁ cos θ₁ = P₁ cos θ₂. II. P₃ = P₁ cos θ₁ + P₂ cos θ₂. III. P₁ sin θ₁ = P₂ sin θ₂.
questions.ai_explanation: Horizontal equilibrium gives P₃ = P₁ cos θ₁ + P₂ cos θ₂. Vertical equilibrium gives P₁ sin θ₁ = P₂ sin θ₂. Statement I is not a general equilibrium identity: the two angles need not be equal. Therefore II and III must hold.
questions.explanation: Horizontal equilibrium gives P₃ = P₁ cos θ₁ + P₂ cos θ₂. Vertical equilibrium gives P₁ sin θ₁ = P₂ sin θ₂. Statement I is not a general equilibrium identity: the two angles need not be equal. Therefore II and III must hold.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A brick at rest on a horizontal table is pulled horizontally to the right by a cord. In the usual dry-friction model, which statement about the friction force on the brick is correct?

options.A: It increases if the pull increases while the brick remains at rest
options.B: It acts horizontally to the right
options.C: It decreases if an identical brick is placed on top while the pull is unchanged
options.D: It is zero once the brick slides
options.E: It changes merely because the brick is turned onto another face while the pull and surface properties stay unchanged

questions.ai_explanation: While the brick remains at rest, static friction acts leftwards and matches the rightward pull. Increasing that pull increases static friction until its limiting value is reached. The limiting value can change with normal force, but the actual static friction still balances the applied pull.
questions.explanation: While the brick remains at rest, static friction acts leftwards and matches the rightward pull. Increasing that pull increases static friction until its limiting value is reached. The limiting value can change with normal force, but the actual static friction still balances the applied pull.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements about liquid pressure is NOT correct? The pressure

options.A: At a point in a liquid is proportional to the depth.
options.B: At any point in a liquid is the same at the same level.
options.C: Is exerted equally in all directions at any point.
options.D: Of a liquid at any point on the wall of its container acts in a direction perpendicular to the wall.
options.E: At a particular depth depends on the shape of the vessel.

questions.ai_explanation: For a liquid at rest, pressure due to the liquid is p = ρgh. At a given depth it depends on density and depth, not on the shape of the container.
questions.explanation: For a liquid at rest, pressure due to the liquid is p = ρgh. At a given depth it depends on density and depth, not on the shape of the container.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statements about defects of vision are correct? I. For a long-sighted person, close objects appear blurred. II. For a short-sighted person, distant objects appear blurred. III. Short sight is corrected using converging lenses.
questions.ai_explanation: Long-sightedness makes close objects difficult to focus on; short-sightedness makes distant objects blurred. Short-sightedness is corrected using diverging lenses, so I and II are correct but III is false.
questions.explanation: Long-sightedness makes close objects difficult to focus on; short-sightedness makes distant objects blurred. Short-sightedness is corrected using diverging lenses, so I and II are correct but III is false.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The range of wavelengths of the visible spectrum is 400nm – 700nm. The wavelength of gamma rays is
questions.ai_explanation: Gamma rays have much shorter wavelengths than visible light. Their wavelengths are therefore shorter than 400 nm.
questions.explanation: Gamma rays have much shorter wavelengths than visible light. Their wavelengths are therefore shorter than 400 nm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If the pressure on 100 cm³ of an ideal gas is doubled while its kelvin temperature is halved, what is the new volume?
questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, PV/T is constant. V₂ = V₁(P₁/P₂)(T₂/T₁) = 100 × ½ × ½ = 25 cm³. Both changes reduce the volume.
questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, PV/T is constant. V₂ = V₁(P₁/P₂)(T₂/T₁) = 100 × ½ × ½ = 25 cm³. Both changes reduce the volume.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following arrangements in the sequence shown can be used to obtain a pure spectrum of white light?

options.A: Source, slit, converging lens, prism, converging lens, screen.
options.C: Source, converging lens, prism, diverging lens, screen.
options.D: Source, slit, prism, diverging lens, screen

questions.ai_explanation: The slit provides a narrow source. The first converging lens makes the rays parallel before the prism separates the colours; the second converging lens focuses them onto the screen to form a pure spectrum.
questions.explanation: The slit provides a narrow source. The first converging lens makes the rays parallel before the prism separates the colours; the second converging lens focuses them onto the screen to form a pure spectrum.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: It is usual to transmit electric power at high voltage and low current. Which of the following are possible advantages of the method. I Heat losses are reduced because the currents are small. II Thin wires can be used because small currents are flowing. III The power can flow faster because the voltage is high.
questions.ai_explanation: For a given transmitted power, a higher voltage requires a smaller current. Heating loss is I²R, so a smaller current reduces heating and allows a smaller conductor cross-section for the same loss limit. Higher voltage does not mean that power travels faster.
questions.explanation: For a given transmitted power, a higher voltage requires a smaller current. Heating loss is I²R, so a smaller current reduces heating and allows a smaller conductor cross-section for the same loss limit. Higher voltage does not mean that power travels faster.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The linear expansivity of brass is 2 × 10⁻⁵ °C⁻¹. If a piece of brass has volume 10 cm³ at 0 °C, what is its volume at 100 °C?
questions.ai_explanation: For a solid, volume expansivity is approximately 3α. V = V₀(1 + 3αΔT) = 10(1 + 3 × 2 × 10⁻⁵ × 100) = 10.06 cm³.
questions.explanation: For a solid, volume expansivity is approximately 3α. V = V₀(1 + 3αΔT) = 10(1 + 3 × 2 × 10⁻⁵ × 100) = 10.06 cm³.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 24 V potential difference is applied across four 6 Ω resistors connected in parallel. What is the current in each resistor?
questions.ai_explanation: Each parallel branch has the full 24 V across it. The current in each 6 Ω resistor is I = V/R = 24/6 = 4 A. The total current through all four branches is 16 A.
questions.explanation: Each parallel branch has the full 24 V across it. The current in each 6 Ω resistor is I = V/R = 24/6 = 4 A. The total current through all four branches is 16 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The electrochemical equivalent of a metal is 0.126 × 10⁻⁶ kg/C. What mass of metal will a current of 5 A deposit from a suitable bath in 1 hour?
questions.ai_explanation: The charge passed is Q = It = 5 × 3600 = 18000 C. Deposited mass m = ZQ = 0.126 × 10⁻⁶ × 18000 = 2.268 × 10⁻³ kg.
questions.explanation: The charge passed is Q = It = 5 × 3600 = 18000 C. Deposited mass m = ZQ = 0.126 × 10⁻⁶ × 18000 = 2.268 × 10⁻³ kg.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Ripples on water are similar to light waves in that they both
questions.ai_explanation: Both water ripples and light can change direction through refraction and spread around edges or openings through diffraction. They do not need to have the same speed or wavelength to show these wave behaviours.
questions.explanation: Both water ripples and light can change direction through refraction and spread around edges or openings through diffraction. They do not need to have the same speed or wavelength to show these wave behaviours.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: 1000 identical drops of oil of density 500 kg/m³ have a total mass of 5 × 10⁻⁴ kg. One drop forms a thin film of area 0.5 m² on water. What is the film thickness?
questions.ai_explanation: One drop has mass (5 × 10⁻⁴)/1000 = 5 × 10⁻⁷ kg. Its volume is m/ρ = 10⁻⁹ m³. Film thickness = volume/area = 10⁻⁹/0.5 = 2 × 10⁻⁹ m.
questions.explanation: One drop has mass (5 × 10⁻⁴)/1000 = 5 × 10⁻⁷ kg. Its volume is m/ρ = 10⁻⁹ m³. Film thickness = volume/area = 10⁻⁹/0.5 = 2 × 10⁻⁹ m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A spring has total length 14 cm when a mass of 20 g is hung from it, and length 16 cm when a mass of 30 g is hung from it. Calculate the unstretched length, assuming Hooke’s law is obeyed.
questions.ai_explanation: Hooke’s law makes extension proportional to load. An extra 10 g increases the length by 2 cm, so the 20 g load produces a 4 cm extension. The natural length is 14 − 4 = 10 cm.
questions.explanation: Hooke’s law makes extension proportional to load. An extra 10 g increases the length by 2 cm, so the 20 g load produces a 4 cm extension. The natural length is 14 − 4 = 10 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statement is correct? I. Mass number equals the total number of protons and electrons in an atom. II. Atomic number equals the number of protons in an atom. III. The number of electrons in an atom equals the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
questions.ai_explanation: Atomic number is the number of protons, so II is correct. Mass number counts protons plus neutrons. A neutral atom has equal numbers of electrons and protons, not protons plus neutrons.
questions.explanation: Atomic number is the number of protons, so II is correct. Mass number counts protons plus neutrons. A neutral atom has equal numbers of electrons and protons, not protons plus neutrons.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A current of 3 A flows for 10 seconds through a 20 Ω heating element embedded in 1000 g of oil, raising the oil temperature by 10 °C. Assuming the electrical energy heats the oil, what is its specific heat capacity?
questions.ai_explanation: Electrical energy supplied is I²Rt = 3² × 20 × 10 = 1800 J. Using Q = mcΔT, c = 1800/(1000 × 10) = 0.18 J/(g·°C), equivalent to 180 J/(kg·°C).
questions.explanation: Electrical energy supplied is I²Rt = 3² × 20 × 10 = 1800 J. Using Q = mcΔT, c = 1800/(1000 × 10) = 0.18 J/(g·°C), equivalent to 180 J/(kg·°C).

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A cell has an open-circuit terminal voltage of 2.2 V. When a 4 Ω resistor is connected across it, the terminal voltage falls to 2.0 V. What is the internal resistance?
questions.ai_explanation: The current through the external resistor is I = 2/4 = 0.5 A. The internal voltage drop is 2.2 − 2.0 = 0.2 V, so internal resistance r = 0.2/0.5 = 0.40 Ω.
questions.explanation: The current through the external resistor is I = 2/4 = 0.5 A. The internal voltage drop is 2.2 − 2.0 = 0.2 V, so internal resistance r = 0.2/0.5 = 0.40 Ω.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: QR is a vertical straight conductor, with Q above R. Current flows upwards from R to Q. Point P lies south of the wire in a horizontal plane. What is the direction of the magnetic field at P due to this current?
questions.ai_explanation: Point your right thumb upwards along the current. Your curled fingers show the magnetic-field direction around the wire. At a point south of the wire the tangent to this circle points east, so the field at P is eastwards.
questions.explanation: Point your right thumb upwards along the current. Your curled fingers show the magnetic-field direction around the wire. At a point south of the wire the tangent to this circle points east, so the field at P is eastwards.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the energy changes which take place when a steam engine drives a generator which lights a lamp?

options.C: Heat → kinetic energy → electricity → heat and light

questions.ai_explanation: The steam engine changes thermal energy into mechanical motion. The generator changes that motion into electrical energy, and the lamp changes electrical energy into light and heat.
questions.explanation: The steam engine changes thermal energy into mechanical motion. The generator changes that motion into electrical energy, and the lamp changes electrical energy into light and heat.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A horizontal copper–steel bimetallic strip is fixed at its left end P and free at its right end Q. Copper is above steel. A fixed contact is just above Q; the battery, bell, fixed contact and strip form a series circuit with an open gap at Q. The linear expansivities are 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ for copper and 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ for steel. Which statements describe the switching action on heating? I. The arrangement bends away from the contact and cannot close the gap. II. The arrangement bends towards the contact and closes the gap. III. Interchanging the metal layers makes the strip bend towards the contact, allowing the gap to close.
questions.ai_explanation: Copper expands more than steel, so it becomes the outside of the bend. With copper above steel, the free end bends downwards towards the steel side, away from the contact above. Reversing the layers makes it bend upwards, allowing contact. Thus I and III are correct.
questions.explanation: Copper expands more than steel, so it becomes the outside of the bend. With copper above steel, the free end bends downwards towards the steel side, away from the contact above. Reversing the layers makes it bend upwards, allowing contact. Thus I and III are correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following may be used to determine relative humidity in a physics laboratory? I Manometer II Wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer III Hair hygrometer IV A hydrometer
questions.ai_explanation: A wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer uses evaporative cooling to determine humidity. A hair hygrometer uses the change in hair length with humidity. A manometer measures pressure; a hydrometer measures liquid density.
questions.explanation: A wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer uses evaporative cooling to determine humidity. A hair hygrometer uses the change in hair length with humidity. A manometer measures pressure; a hydrometer measures liquid density.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a vertical side view, a thin rod PQ lies horizontally on a table. A plane mirror RS slopes downwards to the right, making 45° with the horizontal. Its reflecting face is towards the rod and the observer T, who is to the left of the mirror. What is the orientation of the image of the rod?
questions.ai_explanation: Reflection in a plane mirror preserves length and reverses the component perpendicular to the mirror. Reflecting a horizontal line in a line inclined at 45° changes its orientation to vertical. The image is finite and the same size as the rod.
questions.explanation: Reflection in a plane mirror preserves length and reverses the component perpendicular to the mirror. Reflecting a horizontal line in a line inclined at 45° changes its orientation to vertical. The image is finite and the same size as the rod.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The speed of light in a vacuum is 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. If a transparent liquid has refractive index 4/3, what is the speed of light in the liquid?
questions.ai_explanation: The refractive index is n = c/v. Therefore v = (3.0 × 10⁸)/(4/3) = 2.25 × 10⁸ m/s.
questions.explanation: The refractive index is n = c/v. Therefore v = (3.0 × 10⁸)/(4/3) = 2.25 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A charge of 0.2 C experiences a force of 4 N in an electric field. What is the electric field strength?
questions.ai_explanation: Electric field strength is force per unit charge: E = F/q = 4/0.2 = 20 N/C.
questions.explanation: Electric field strength is force per unit charge: E = F/q = 4/0.2 = 20 N/C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Longitudinal waves do not exhibit
questions.ai_explanation: Polarization requires vibrations perpendicular to the direction of travel. Longitudinal waves vibrate along their direction of travel, so they cannot be polarized.
questions.explanation: Polarization requires vibrations perpendicular to the direction of travel. Longitudinal waves vibrate along their direction of travel, so they cannot be polarized.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An inverted U-tube passes over the rim of an open water tank. Its inlet O is submerged below the water surface W; its other end P is outside the tank and open to the air. For ordinary siphon flow from the tank, which listed conditions are required?

options.A: The tube is completely filled with water and P is higher than W
options.B: P is lower than both O and W
options.C: P is lower than W and O reaches the tank bottom
options.D: The tube is completely filled with water and P is lower than W
options.E: The tube is completely filled with water and O reaches the tank bottom

questions.ai_explanation: A continuous water column must first fill the tube, and the outlet P must be below the tank’s water surface W for gravity to drive outward flow. The inlet O only needs to remain submerged; it need not reach the bottom, and P need not be lower than O.
questions.explanation: A continuous water column must first fill the tube, and the outlet P must be below the tank’s water surface W for gravity to drive outward flow. The inlet O only needs to remain submerged; it need not reach the bottom, and P need not be lower than O.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The distance travelled by a particle starting from rest is plotted against the square of the time elapsed from the commencement of motion. The resulting graph is linear. The slope of this graph is a measure of
questions.ai_explanation: Starting from rest with constant acceleration, s = ½at². A graph of s against t² therefore has slope ½a. Equivalently, if s = kt², differentiating twice gives a = 2k.
questions.explanation: Starting from rest with constant acceleration, s = ½at². A graph of s against t² therefore has slope ½a. Equivalently, if s = kt², differentiating twice gives a = 2k.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental S.I. unit?
questions.ai_explanation: The radian measures plane angle and is a dimensionless derived unit. Metre, ampere, kelvin and second are SI base units.
questions.explanation: The radian measures plane angle and is a dimensionless derived unit. Metre, ampere, kelvin and second are SI base units.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A uniform metre rule PT is horizontal and pivoted at R, its 70 cm mark. A downward force of 0.1 N acts at Q, the 60 cm mark, and a downward force of 0.4 N acts at S, the 85 cm mark. The rule is in equilibrium under these forces, its weight and the pivot reaction. What is its weight?
questions.ai_explanation: The uniform rule’s weight W acts at 50 cm, 20 cm left of the pivot. Taking moments about 70 cm gives 0.4 × 15 = 0.1 × 10 + W × 20, with distances in centimetres. Thus W = (6 − 1)/20 = 0.25 N.
questions.explanation: The uniform rule’s weight W acts at 50 cm, 20 cm left of the pivot. Taking moments about 70 cm gives 0.4 × 15 = 0.1 × 10 + W × 20, with distances in centimetres. Thus W = (6 − 1)/20 = 0.25 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For which quantities are the dimensions ML²T⁻² correct? I. Moment of a force. II. Work. III. Acceleration.
questions.ai_explanation: Force has dimensions MLT⁻². Both moment of force and work multiply force by a distance, giving ML²T⁻². Acceleration has dimensions LT⁻², so I and II are correct.
questions.explanation: Force has dimensions MLT⁻². Both moment of force and work multiply force by a distance, giving ML²T⁻². Acceleration has dimensions LT⁻², so I and II are correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What volume of alcohol of density 8.4 × 10² kg/m³ has the same mass as 4.2 m³ of petrol of density 7.2 × 10² kg/m³?
questions.ai_explanation: The petrol mass is 720 × 4.2 = 3024 kg. For alcohol of density 840 kg/m³, volume = mass/density = 3024/840 = 3.6 m³.
questions.explanation: The petrol mass is 720 × 4.2 = 3024 kg. For alcohol of density 840 kg/m³, volume = mass/density = 3024/840 = 3.6 m³.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For correcting long sight defects in the human eye we require a
questions.ai_explanation: A long-sighted eye does not converge light from close objects sufficiently. A converging lens adds focusing power so that the image forms on the retina.
questions.explanation: A long-sighted eye does not converge light from close objects sufficiently. A converging lens adds focusing power so that the image forms on the retina.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a concave mirror to form a real diminished image, the object must be placed

options.B: Between the mirror and its focus
options.C: Between the focus and the centre of curvature
options.E: At a distance greater than the radius of curvature

questions.ai_explanation: A concave mirror forms a real, smaller image when the object is beyond its centre of curvature. The image then lies between the focus and the centre of curvature.
questions.explanation: A concave mirror forms a real, smaller image when the object is beyond its centre of curvature. The image then lies between the focus and the centre of curvature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The unit of quantity of electricity (electric charge) is called
questions.ai_explanation: Electric charge is measured in coulombs. One coulomb is the charge transferred by a current of one ampere flowing for one second: Q = It.
questions.explanation: Electric charge is measured in coulombs. One coulomb is the charge transferred by a current of one ampere flowing for one second: Q = It.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The resistance of a wire depends on
questions.ai_explanation: For a uniform wire, R = ρL/A. Resistance depends on its length, cross-sectional area (and therefore diameter), and resistivity. Temperature also affects resistivity, so all four factors matter.
questions.explanation: For a uniform wire, R = ρL/A. Resistance depends on its length, cross-sectional area (and therefore diameter), and resistivity. Temperature also affects resistivity, so all four factors matter.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two cells, each of emf 1.5 V and internal resistance 2 Ω, are connected in parallel with matching polarities. What current flows through an external 1 Ω resistor?
questions.ai_explanation: Identical cells in parallel retain emf 1.5 V, while their combined internal resistance is 2/2 = 1 Ω. Including the external resistor, I = 1.5/(1 + 1) = 0.75 A.
questions.explanation: Identical cells in parallel retain emf 1.5 V, while their combined internal resistance is 2/2 = 1 Ω. Including the external resistor, I = 1.5/(1 + 1) = 0.75 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which component is NOT contained in a zinc-carbon dry cell?
questions.ai_explanation: A zinc-carbon dry cell contains a carbon rod, a zinc casing and a paste containing ammonium chloride and manganese dioxide. A copper rod is not one of these components.
questions.explanation: A zinc-carbon dry cell contains a carbon rod, a zinc casing and a paste containing ammonium chloride and manganese dioxide. A copper rod is not one of these components.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following can be described as high tension transmission?
questions.ai_explanation: High-tension transmission means high-voltage transmission. For the same power, using a high voltage permits a low current and reduces I²R heating losses in the conductors.
questions.explanation: High-tension transmission means high-voltage transmission. For the same power, using a high voltage permits a low current and reduces I²R heating losses in the conductors.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: All heat generated in a 5 Ω resistor by a 2 A current flowing for 30 seconds evaporates 5 g of liquid at its boiling point. What is the specific latent heat of the liquid?
questions.ai_explanation: The heat supplied is I²Rt = 2² × 5 × 30 = 600 J. Specific latent heat is energy per unit mass: L = 600/5 = 120 J/g.
questions.explanation: The heat supplied is I²Rt = 2² × 5 × 30 = 600 J. Specific latent heat is energy per unit mass: L = 600/5 = 120 J/g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: When a standing wave occurs in an air column, the distance between a node and its nearest antinode is equal to
questions.ai_explanation: In a standing wave, adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart. An antinode is midway between them, so a node and its nearest antinode are one-quarter wavelength apart.
questions.explanation: In a standing wave, adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart. An antinode is midway between them, so a node and its nearest antinode are one-quarter wavelength apart.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statements are NOT correct? I. At fixed temperature and composition, pressure changes do not affect the speed of sound in air treated as an ideal gas. II. The speed of sound in air increases with temperature. III. The quality of a note depends only on its frequency.
questions.ai_explanation: At fixed temperature and composition, pressure changes do not change the ideal-gas speed of sound. Sound speed increases with temperature. The quality or timbre of a note depends on its mixture of frequencies and their relative amplitudes, so only III is incorrect.
questions.explanation: At fixed temperature and composition, pressure changes do not change the ideal-gas speed of sound. Sound speed increases with temperature. The quality or timbre of a note depends on its mixture of frequencies and their relative amplitudes, so only III is incorrect.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two identical tuning forks have natural frequency 256 Hz. One is loaded, and 4 beats per second are heard when they sound together. What is the frequency of the loaded fork?
questions.ai_explanation: Adding a small load to a tuning fork lowers its frequency. The beat frequency is the difference between the two frequencies, so the loaded fork vibrates at 256 − 4 = 252 Hz.
questions.explanation: Adding a small load to a tuning fork lowers its frequency. The beat frequency is the difference between the two frequencies, so the loaded fork vibrates at 256 − 4 = 252 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Dew point is the temperature at which water vapour in the atmosphere

options.D: Is just sufficient to cause cooling
options.E: Has a relative humidity of fifty percent

questions.ai_explanation: The dew point is the temperature to which air must be cooled, without changing its water-vapour content, to become saturated and start forming liquid droplets.
questions.explanation: The dew point is the temperature to which air must be cooled, without changing its water-vapour content, to become saturated and start forming liquid droplets.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The lower (0 °C) and upper (100 °C) fixed points of a mercury-in-glass thermometer are 210 mm apart. In a room, the mercury ends 49 mm above the lower point. What is the room temperature to one decimal place?
questions.ai_explanation: The 210 mm interval represents 100 °C. A rise of 49 mm therefore corresponds to (49/210) × 100 = 23.33… °C, or 23.3 °C to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: The 210 mm interval represents 100 °C. A rise of 49 mm therefore corresponds to (49/210) × 100 = 23.33… °C, or 23.3 °C to one decimal place.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If a solid changes directly into a gas when heat is applied the process is called
questions.ai_explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without passing through a liquid phase. Dry ice is a familiar example.
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without passing through a liquid phase. Dry ice is a familiar example.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Heat is supplied at 100 W to 1.0 × 10⁻² kg of liquid for 20 seconds. Its temperature rises by 5 °C. Assuming the supplied heat warms the liquid, what is its specific heat capacity?
questions.ai_explanation: Heat supplied is Pt = 100 × 20 = 2000 J. The temperature rise is 5 K, so c = Q/(mΔT) = 2000/(0.01 × 5) = 4.0 × 10⁴ J/(kg·K).
questions.explanation: Heat supplied is Pt = 100 × 20 = 2000 J. The temperature rise is 5 K, so c = Q/(mΔT) = 2000/(0.01 × 5) = 4.0 × 10⁴ J/(kg·K).

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Between terminals X and Y, a 4 μF capacitor connects X to an intermediate node. From that node to Y are three parallel branches containing a 4 μF, a 3 μF and a 2 μF capacitor respectively. What is the effective capacitance between X and Y?
questions.ai_explanation: The three parallel capacitors add to 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 μF. This 9 μF combination is in series with the first 4 μF capacitor, giving C = (4 × 9)/(4 + 9) = 36/13 μF = 2 10/13 μF.
questions.explanation: The three parallel capacitors add to 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 μF. This 9 μF combination is in series with the first 4 μF capacitor, giving C = (4 × 9)/(4 + 9) = 36/13 μF = 2 10/13 μF.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a model atmosphere, sea-level pressure is 10⁵ N/m², density is uniform at 1 kg/m³, and g = 10 m/s². What is the height of this atmosphere?
questions.ai_explanation: For the stated uniform-density model, p = ρgh. Hence h = 10⁵/(1 × 10) = 10000 m. This is the height of the simplified model atmosphere.
questions.explanation: For the stated uniform-density model, p = ρgh. Hence h = 10⁵/(1 × 10) = 10000 m. This is the height of the simplified model atmosphere.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct explanation of the inertia of a body?

options.A: Ability to overcome the earth’s gravity
options.D: Reluctance to start moving and its readiness to stop moving once it has begun to move
options.E: Reluctance to start moving and its reluctance to stop moving once it has begun to move.

questions.ai_explanation: Inertia is resistance to a change in velocity. A body tends to stay at rest or continue moving with constant velocity unless a resultant external force acts.
questions.explanation: Inertia is resistance to a change in velocity. A body tends to stay at rest or continue moving with constant velocity unless a resultant external force acts.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A water pump at Kainji Dam lifts 1000 kg of water through a vertical height of 10 m in 10 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is its useful lifting power?
questions.ai_explanation: The gain in gravitational potential energy is mgh = 1000 × 10 × 10 = 100000 J. Dividing by 10 s gives 10000 W = 10 kW of useful lifting power.
questions.explanation: The gain in gravitational potential energy is mgh = 1000 × 10 × 10 = 100000 J. Dividing by 10 s gives 10000 W = 10 kW of useful lifting power.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What is the apparent colour of a RED SHIRT when viewed in PURE green light?
questions.ai_explanation: In the ideal colour model, a red shirt reflects red light and absorbs green light. Under pure green illumination there is no red light to reflect, so it appears black.
questions.explanation: In the ideal colour model, a red shirt reflects red light and absorbs green light. Under pure green illumination there is no red light to reflect, so it appears black.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which list gives the colours of the visible spectrum in order from longest to shortest wavelength?

options.A: Blue, red, green. Yellow, indigo, violet, orange.
options.B: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.
options.C: Red, orange, yellow, indigo, green, blue, violet.
options.D: Indigo, green, blue, violet, yellow, red, orange.
options.E: Yellow, blue, green, violet, orange, indigo, red.

questions.ai_explanation: From longest to shortest visible wavelength, the usual order is red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. Frequency increases in the reverse direction to wavelength.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Cathode rays are
questions.ai_explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons. They carry negative charge and can be deflected by electric and magnetic fields.
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons. They carry negative charge and can be deflected by electric and magnetic fields.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Radio waves travel at 3 × 10⁸ m/s. A station broadcasts at 800 kHz. What is the wavelength?
questions.ai_explanation: Convert 800 kHz to 800000 Hz. Wavelength λ = v/f = (3 × 10⁸)/800000 = 375 m.

questions.question: Air trapped above a mercury barometer makes it read 73.5 cm when the true height is 75.0 cm. The trapped air volume is 8.0 cm³. At the same temperature, it later reads 74.0 cm and the trapped volume is 6.0 cm³. Find the true barometric height.

questions.explanation: Initially the trapped air pressure is 75.0 − 73.5 = 1.5 cmHg. At constant temperature, p₂ = 1.5 × 8/6 = 2.0 cmHg. True atmospheric pressure is then 74.0 + 2.0 = 76.0 cmHg.

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Calculate the heat required to convert 2 kg of ice at −2 °C to water at 0 °C. The specific heat capacity of ice is 2090 J/(kg·°C), and its specific latent heat of fusion is 333 kJ/kg.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In which of the following are the substances arranged in descending order of their thermal conductivities?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: At a place with magnetic declination 10°E, a compass reads N40°E. What is the true geographic bearing?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Capacitors of 6 μF and 8 μF are in series. What additional capacitor, connected in series with them, gives a total capacitance of 3 μF?

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statement is true of the ordinary single-photon photoelectric effect?

questions.question: What liquid-column height supports atmospheric pressure 102000 N/m² if liquid density is 2600 kg/m³ and g = 10 m/s²? Give the answer to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A platinum wire has resistance 0.75 Ω at 0 °C and 1.05 Ω at 100 °C. Assuming linear variation, find its temperature when resistance is 0.90 Ω.

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In ordinary heat-transfer experiments, which statements are correct? I. Land and sea breezes are natural convection currents. II. questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Geometrical shadows and eclipses result primarily from the

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object 3 cm high is placed vertically 10 cm in front of a concave mirror. Its image is 40 cm from the mirror. Find the magnitude of the image height.
questions.ai_explanation: The magnitude of magnification is image distance divided by object distance: 40/10 = 4. Therefore the image height has magnitude 4 × 3 = 12 cm.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of magnification is image distance divided by object distance: 40/10 = 4. Therefore the image height has magnitude 4 × 3 = 12 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What must be the distance between an object and a converging lens of focal length 20cm to produce an erect image two times the object height?
questions.ai_explanation: An erect image from a converging lens is virtual: v = −2u. Substituting in 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/20 = 1/(2u). Hence u = 10 cm, inside the focal length.
questions.explanation: An erect image from a converging lens is virtual: v = −2u. Substituting in 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/20 = 1/(2u). Hence u = 10 cm, inside the focal length.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In an uncorrected short-sighted eye, light rays from a point on a very distant object are focused

options.C: Behind the retina by a diverging lens

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Under white illumination, which primary colour does an ideal magenta surface absorb?
questions.ai_explanation: An ideal magenta surface reflects red and blue light and absorbs green. Under white illumination, the reflected red and blue combine to appear magenta.
questions.explanation: An ideal magenta surface reflects red and blue light and absorbs green. Under white illumination, the reflected red and blue combine to appear magenta.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a resonance tube closed at one end, the first resonant air-column length is 20 cm for a 480 Hz tuning fork. Neglect end correction and find the speed of sound.
questions.ai_explanation: At the first resonance of a tube closed at one end, L = λ/4. Thus λ = 4 × 0.20 = 0.80 m and v = fλ = 480 × 0.80 = 384 m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An organ pipe closed at one end is 80 cm long. Neglect end correction. Find its fundamental frequency to the nearest hertz if sound speed is 340 m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Three identical cells, each of emf 1.5 V and internal resistance 1.0 Ω, are connected in parallel with matching polarity across a 2.67 Ω load. Find the load current to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: Identical cells in parallel retain emf 1.5 V and have internal resistance 1/3 Ω. The load current is 1.5/(2.67 + 1/3) = 0.4994… A, or 0.50 A to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The energy supplied by an electrical source per unit positive charge for a complete circuit is its

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is an essential physical property of the wires used for making fuses?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For the same transmitted power, using a higher voltage reduces energy lost in the transmission wires through
questions.ai_explanation: For the same transmitted power, increasing voltage reduces current because P = VI. Heating loss in the wires is I²R, so lowering current reduces heat dissipation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A galvanometer with full-scale current 10 mA and coil resistance 30 Ω is converted to a 10 A ammeter. Which approximate resistor and connection are required?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What precaution should a manufacturer take to ensure that energy loss in a transformer is minimized?

questions.question: An object moves with uniform speed round a circle. Its acceleration has

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: At normal atmospheric pressure, how much more heat is released by 4 kg of steam at 100 °C than by 4 kg of water at 100 °C when each ends as water at 80 °C? Use latent heat 2260000 J/kg and water specific heat 4200 J/(kg·K).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is CORRECT about the earth’s magnetic field?

questions.question: A ruler has divisions 1 cm apart. A single reading is rounded to the nearest division. What is the maximum magnitude of rounding error? Ignore other measurement errors.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a simple pendulum undergoing small oscillations, which quantities affect its period? I. Bob mass. II. Pendulum length. III. Gravitational acceleration.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In an experiment measuring Young’s modulus of a circular wire, the tensile stress depends on the

options.C: Radius of the wire and extension
options.D: Extension and original length of the wire

questions.ai_explanation: Tensile stress is force divided by cross-sectional area. For a circular wire, stress =F/(πr²), so the load and radius determine it. Extension and original length instead determine strain.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If a plastic sphere floats in water (density = 1000 kg m-3) with 0.5 of its volume submerged and floats in oil with 0.4 volume submerged, the density of the oil is

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: At constant pressure, the density of a fixed mass of ideal gas is

options.C: Inversely proportional to its absolute temperature

questions.ai_explanation: At constant pressure, a fixed amount of ideal gas satisfies V/T =constant. Since density is mass divided by volume, density is inversely proportional to absolute temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: How much heat is absorbed by 0.05 kg of copper, of specific heat capacity 390 J/(kg·K), when heated from 20 °C to 70 °C?
questions.ai_explanation: The temperature rise is 70 −20 =50 K. Heat absorbed is mcΔT =0.05 ×390 ×50 =975 J =9.75 ×10² J.
questions.explanation: The temperature rise is 70 −20 =50 K. Heat absorbed is mcΔT =0.05 ×390 ×50 =975 J =9.75 ×10² J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following characteristics of a wave is used in the measurement of the depth of the sea?
questions.ai_explanation: Echo sounding sends a sound pulse downward and measures its return after reflection from the seabed. With sound speed v and round-trip time t, depth is vt/2.
questions.explanation: Echo sounding sends a sound pulse downward and measures its return after reflection from the seabed. With sound speed v and round-trip time t, depth is vt/2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A siren disc has 32 equally spaced holes in one ring. A single air jet produces one pulse per passing hole. If the disc rotates at 25 revolutions per second, what is the sound frequency?
questions.ai_explanation: Each revolution lets 32 holes pass the air jet, producing 32 pressure pulses. At 25 revolutions per second, the pulse frequency is 32 ×25 =800 Hz.
questions.explanation: Each revolution lets 32 holes pass the air jet, producing 32 pressure pulses. At 25 revolutions per second, the pulse frequency is 32 ×25 =800 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following properties make the convex mirror useful as a driving mirror? I The image is real II The image is erect III It has a wide field of view IV The image is magnified
questions.ai_explanation: For objects in front of it, a convex mirror gives virtual, upright, diminished images. Its wide field of view lets a driver see more of the surrounding traffic. Therefore II and III apply.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object is placed between the pole and focus of a concave mirror. The virtual image obtained is
questions.ai_explanation: An object between a concave mirror and its focus produces a virtual image behind the mirror. The image is upright and larger than the object.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The speed of light in air is 3.0 ×10⁸ m/s. Find its speed in glass of refractive index 1.50 relative to air.
questions.ai_explanation: The refractive index is the speed in air divided by the speed in glass. Thus v =3.0 ×10⁸/1.50 =2.0 ×10⁸ m/s.
questions.explanation: The refractive index is the speed in air divided by the speed in glass. Thus v =3.0 ×10⁸/1.50 =2.0 ×10⁸ m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which arrangement gives the conventional order of these electromagnetic bands from shorter to longer typical wavelengths?

options.C: Infra-red rays, ultraviolet rays, x-rays, gamma rays.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The angle between the direction of the earth’s magnetic field and the horizontal is called the

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Find the magnitude of the force on an electron of charge−1.6 ×10⁻¹⁹ C in an electric field of magnitude 10⁸ V/m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which change does not alter the equilibrium emf of a primary cell, with chemistry and other conditions otherwise unchanged?
questions.ai_explanation: Cell emf depends on electrode reactions, electrolyte conditions and temperature. Scaling up an otherwise identical cell increases available charge and can change internal resistance, but does not change its equilibrium emf.
questions.explanation: Cell emf depends on electrode reactions, electrolyte conditions and temperature. Scaling up an otherwise identical cell increases available charge and can change internal resistance, but does not change its equilibrium emf.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 5 V battery is connected across an initially uncharged 2.0 μF capacitor. After a long time, what is the magnitude of charge on either plate?
questions.ai_explanation: Charge magnitude on either plate is Q =CV =(2.0 ×10⁻⁶) ×5 =10 ×10⁻⁶ C =10 μC. The two plates carry equal and opposite charges.
questions.explanation: Charge magnitude on either plate is Q =CV =(2.0 ×10⁻⁶) ×5 =10 ×10⁻⁶ C =10 μC. The two plates carry equal and opposite charges.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For resistive devices with the same proportional protection margin, which has the smallest operating current and therefore needs the lowest fuse current rating?
questions.ai_explanation: Operating current is P/V. The four currents are 0.25 A,1.5 A,3.33 A and 8 A. The 60 W,240 V device draws the smallest current and needs the lowest current rating when the same protection margin is used.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For steady current I through a constant resistance R for time t, the heat produced is

options.A: Inversely proportional to the current and the resistance
options.B: Directly proportional to the current, resistance and the time.
options.C: Inversely proportional to the square of the resistance, current and the time.
options.D: Directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance and the time.

questions.ai_explanation: Joule heating is H =I²Rt for a steady current through a constant resistance. Heat is proportional to current squared, resistance and elapsed time.
questions.explanation: Joule heating is H =I²Rt for a steady current through a constant resistance. Heat is proportional to current squared, resistance and elapsed time.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A galvanometer has resistance 10 Ω and full-scale current 0.05 A. What added resistance converts it into a 100 V voltmeter, and how is it connected?
questions.ai_explanation: The total required resistance is V/I =100/0.05 =2000 Ω. Subtracting the galvanometer’s 10 Ω gives R =1990 Ω. It is connected in series to limit the current through the meter.
questions.explanation: The total required resistance is V/I =100/0.05 =2000 Ω. Subtracting the galvanometer’s 10 Ω gives R =1990 Ω. It is connected in series to limit the current through the meter.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The units of impedance, RMS voltage and resonance frequency are respectively
questions.ai_explanation: Impedance is voltage divided by current, so its unit is the ohm. RMS voltage is measured in volts, and resonance frequency in hertz, or cycles per second.
questions.explanation: Impedance is voltage divided by current, so its unit is the ohm. RMS voltage is measured in volts, and resonance frequency in hertz, or cycles per second.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a sinusoidal alternating current with peak I₀, which relation gives its RMS current Iᵣₘₛ?
questions.ai_explanation: For sinusoidal current, the mean of sin² over a cycle is 1/2. Thus the mean square current is I₀²/2, and its square root is Iᵣₘₛ =I₀/√2.
questions.explanation: For sinusoidal current, the mean of sin² over a cycle is 1/2. Thus the mean square current is I₀²/2, and its square root is Iᵣₘₛ =I₀/√2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following quantities has the same unit as the watt?
questions.ai_explanation: A watt is a joule per second. Force multiplied by velocity has units N·m/s =J/s =W, so it has the unit of power.
questions.explanation: A watt is a joule per second. Force multiplied by velocity has units N·m/s =J/s =W, so it has the unit of power.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two forces of 7 N and 3 N act at right angles. If θ is the angle between the resultant and the 7 N force, which relation holds?
questions.ai_explanation: The resultant has components 7 N along the larger force and 3 N perpendicular to it. Therefore tan θ =opposite/adjacent =3/7.
questions.explanation: The resultant has components 7 N along the larger force and 3 N perpendicular to it. Therefore tan θ =opposite/adjacent =3/7.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object is projected at 80 m/s,30° above horizontal. Neglect air resistance and use g =10 m/s². Find its maximum height above the launch point.
questions.ai_explanation: The initial upward velocity is 80 sin 30° =40 m/s. At maximum height the vertical velocity is zero, so h =40²/(2 ×10) =80 m.
questions.explanation: The initial upward velocity is 80 sin 30° =40 m/s. At maximum height the vertical velocity is zero, so h =40²/(2 ×10) =80 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An aeroplane lands at 180 km/h and slows uniformly to rest in 30 s. What distance does it cover before stopping?
questions.ai_explanation: The landing speed is 180/3.6 =50 m/s. Uniform deceleration gives average speed(50 +0)/2 =25 m/s, so distance is 25 ×30 =750 m.
questions.explanation: The landing speed is 180/3.6 =50 m/s. Uniform deceleration gives average speed(50 +0)/2 =25 m/s, so distance is 25 ×30 =750 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A particle moves in a fixed horizontal circle at constant angular velocity. Which statement is true?

options.A: Kinetic energy is constant but linear momentum varies
options.B: Linear momentum is constant but kinetic energy varies
options.C: Kinetic energy and linear momentum are both constant
options.D: Speed and linear velocity are both constant

questions.ai_explanation: At constant angular velocity on a fixed circle, speed is constant, so kinetic energy stays constant. The direction of velocity changes continuously, making linear momentum change direction.
questions.explanation: At constant angular velocity on a fixed circle, speed is constant, so kinetic energy stays constant. The direction of velocity changes continuously, making linear momentum change direction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Starting with water stored at height, which sequence describes the main energy conversions when a hydroelectric station powers a lamp?
questions.ai_explanation: Water stored above a turbine has gravitational potential energy. Flowing water turns the turbine, which drives a generator. Electrical energy from the generator is then converted to light by a lamp.
questions.explanation: Water stored above a turbine has gravitational potential energy. Flowing water turns the turbine, which drives a generator. Electrical energy from the generator is then converted to light by a lamp.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object of mass 400 g and density 600 kg/m³ hangs at rest from a string with half its volume immersed in paraffin of density 900 kg/m³. Find the string tension. Use g =10 m/s².
questions.ai_explanation: The object weighs 0.4 ×10 =4 N. Half its volume displaces paraffin of mass 0.5 ×0.4 ×900/600 =0.3 kg, giving 3 N upthrust. The string tension is 4 −3 =1 N.
questions.explanation: The object weighs 0.4 ×10 =4 N. Half its volume displaces paraffin of mass 0.5 ×0.4 ×900/600 =0.3 kg, giving 3 N upthrust. The string tension is 4 −3 =1 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: With its reference-junction temperature fixed, a thermocouple measures temperature through changes in its

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A fixed mass of ideal gas has its volume halved and absolute temperature doubled. What happens to its pressure?
questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, P is proportional toT/V. Doubling absolute temperature while halving volume multiplies pressure by 2/(1/2) =4.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Mix 200 g of water at 90 °C with 100 g of water at 30 °C. Neglect heat loss and the container’s heat capacity. What is the final temperature?
questions.ai_explanation: Ignoring heat loss, heat lost by hot water equals heat gained by cool water:200(90 −T) =100(T −30). Solving gives 300 T =21000, so T =70 °C.
questions.explanation: Ignoring heat loss, heat lost by hot water equals heat gained by cool water:200(90 −T) =100(T −30). Solving gives 300 T =21000, so T =70 °C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A solid melts at 80 °C. At that temperature,10⁵ J melts 10 g of the solid. Find its specific latent heat of fusion.
questions.ai_explanation: At the melting point, heat goes into the phase change. The mass is 10 g =0.010 kg, so specific latent heat is Q/m =10⁵/0.010 =1.00 ×10⁷ J/kg.
questions.explanation: At the melting point, heat goes into the phase change. The mass is 10 g =0.010 kg, so specific latent heat is Q/m =10⁵/0.010 =1.00 ×10⁷ J/kg.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A stationary wave has wavelength 60 cm. Find the distance between consecutive antinodes.
questions.ai_explanation: Consecutive antinodes of a stationary wave are half a wavelength apart. Their separation is therefore 60/2 =30 cm.
questions.explanation: Consecutive antinodes of a stationary wave are half a wavelength apart. Their separation is therefore 60/2 =30 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following waves can propagate through a vacuum?

questions.explanation: Infrared radiation is electromagnetic and can travel through vacuum. Sound, ultrasound and other acoustic waves need a material medium for their pressure disturbances.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A radar pulse returns to its transmitting antenna 4 ×10⁻³ s after reflection from an aircraft. How far away is the aircraft? Use c =3 ×10⁸ m/s.
questions.ai_explanation: The measured time includes the outward and return journeys. One-way distance is ct/2 =(3 ×10⁸)(4 ×10⁻³)/2 =6 ×10⁵ m =6 ×10² km.
questions.explanation: The measured time includes the outward and return journeys. One-way distance is ct/2 =(3 ×10⁸)(4 ×10⁻³)/2 =6 ×10⁵ m =6 ×10² km.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A concave mirror of radius r forms a real image. Let u and v be the positive object and image distances. Which expression gives the magnitude of linear magnification?
questions.ai_explanation: For a real image, magnification magnitude is v/u. Since 1/u +1/v =2/r, multiplying byv gives v/u +1 =2 v/r. Therefore magnification magnitude is 2 v/r −1.
questions.explanation: For a real image, magnification magnitude is v/u. Since 1/u +1/v =2/r, multiplying byv gives v/u +1 =2 v/r. Therefore magnification magnitude is 2 v/r −1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A thin camera lens has focal length 20 cm. An object is 100 cm from the lens. What lens-to-film distance gives a sharp image?
questions.ai_explanation: Using 1/f =1/u +1/v gives 1/v =1/20 −1/100 =1/25. The film must therefore be 25 cm from the lens to receive the sharp real image.
questions.explanation: Using 1/f =1/u +1/v gives 1/v =1/20 −1/100 =1/25. The film must therefore be 25 cm from the lens to receive the sharp real image.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following correctly explain(s) why soft iron is preferred to steel in electromagnets? I Soft iron is more readily magnetized than steel. II Soft iron is more readily demagnetized than steel. III Soft iron retains magnetism more than steel.
questions.ai_explanation: Soft iron magnetizes readily when current flows and loses most of that magnetism when current stops. These properties make the electromagnet easy to switch on and off. Steel retains more magnetism.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The terminal voltage of a battery is 4.0 V when supplying a current of 2.0 A, and 2.0 V when supplying a current of 3.0 A. The internal resistance of the battery is
questions.ai_explanation: Terminal voltage is V =E −Ir. The voltage falls by 4 −2 =2 V when current rises by 3 −2 =1 A. Thus r =2/1 =2 Ω; both measurements then give emf 8 V.
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage is V =E −Ir. The voltage falls by 4 −2 =2 V when current rises by 3 −2 =1 A. Thus r =2/1 =2 Ω; both measurements then give emf 8 V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 12 V ideal battery supplies a 1 Ω resistor in series with two parallel branches. Each branch contains two 2 Ω resistors in series. What is the total current supplied by the battery?
questions.ai_explanation: Each parallel branch has two 2 Ω resistors in series, giving 4 Ω per branch. Their parallel equivalent is 2 Ω. Adding the 1 Ω series resistor gives 3 Ω, so battery current is 12/3 =4 A.
questions.explanation: Each parallel branch has two 2 Ω resistors in series, giving 4 Ω per branch. Their parallel equivalent is 2 Ω. Adding the 1 Ω series resistor gives 3 Ω, so battery current is 12/3 =4 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 24 V ideal battery is connected across two parallel branches. One branch contains 5 μF and 15 μF capacitors in series; the other contains a 20 μF capacitor. All are initially uncharged. After charging, what is the voltage across the 5 μF capacitor?
questions.ai_explanation: The 5 μF and 15 μF capacitors are in series across 24 V. Their voltage drops are inversely proportional to capacitance, so the 5 μF capacitor gets 15/(5 +15) ×24 =18 V.
questions.explanation: The 5 μF and 15 μF capacitors are in series across 24 V. Their voltage drops are inversely proportional to capacitance, so the 5 μF capacitor gets 15/(5 +15) ×24 =18 V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A resistive instrument rated 40 W has resistance 90 Ω. What operating voltage gives its rated power?

questions.explanation: For a resistive instrument, P =V²/R. Therefore V =√(PR) =√(40 ×90) =√3600 =60 V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a fixed transmitted power, the primary aim of high-voltage transmission is to

options.A: Minimize electrical energy losses due to heat production
options.B: Increase the rate of energy transfer by using high voltage
options.C: Increase the current in the wires.
options.D: Generate electricity at high current and low voltage.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Find the inductive reactance of a 30.0 mH inductor at 1.30 ×10³ Hz, to one decimal place.
questions.ai_explanation: Inductive reactance is Xᴸ =2πfL. Converting 30.0 mH to 0.0300 H gives 2π ×1300 ×0.0300 =245.04… Ω, or 245.0 Ω to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance is Xᴸ =2πfL. Converting 30.0 mH to 0.0300 H gives 2π ×1300 ×0.0300 =245.04… Ω, or 245.0 Ω to one decimal place.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statements correctly describe cathode rays? I. They consist of small negatively charged particles. II. They can be deflected magnetically but not electrically. III. They consist of fast neutrons deflected by an electric field.
questions.ai_explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons, which carry negative charge. An electric field can deflect them, and a magnetic field can deflect them when they have a velocity component perpendicular to it.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In the ordinary photoelectric effect, the threshold frequency depends on the

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: After three half-lives, what fraction of the original radioactive isotope has decayed?

questions.question: A nucleus has atomic number 88 and mass number 226. After two beta-minus decays and one alpha decay, which notation represents the final nucleus?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A uniform horizontal beam of weight 200 N and length 50 m is pivoted at one end. A cord at the other end makes 30° above the beam and holds it in equilibrium. Find the cord tension.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 50 kg object is released from rest 2 m above the ground. Neglect air resistance and use g =10 m/s². Find its kinetic energy just before impact.

questions.explanation: Neglecting air resistance, gravitational potential energy becomes kinetic energy. Thus K =mgh =50 ×10 ×2 =1000 J just before impact.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A horizontal force just starts a 20 kg object sliding on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction is 0.2. Find the force, using g = 10 m/s².

questions.explanation: Just before sliding starts, the limiting friction is μₛN. The horizontal force leaves N = mg, so F = 0.2 × 20 × 10 = 40 N.

questions.question: For a connected liquid of uniform density at rest, neglecting capillary effects, which statements are true? I. Pressure acts equally in all directions at a point. II. questions.question: The mass of a specific gravity bottle is 15.2 g when it is empty. It is 24.8 g when filled with kerosene and 27.2 g when filled with distilled water. Calculate the relative density of kerosene.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A heater melts 100 g of ice at its melting point in 1 minute. Neglect heat losses and the test tube’s heat capacity. Find its power. Use latent heat of fusion 336 J/g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Sound travels from the surface to the sea bottom and returns after 4 s. If its speed is 1500 m/s, find the depth.

questions.question: Which change halves the fundamental frequency of a stretched sonometer wire, with other relevant quantities held constant?

questions.question: To produce a parallel paraxial beam from a concave mirror, where should a small lamp be placed on its principal axis?

questions.question: Light of frequency 6.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz enters stationary glass of refractive index 1.5 from air. Find its frequency in the glass.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A converging thin lens of focal length 20 cm forms a virtual image with magnification 2. Find the object distance.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A plastic pen rubbed with dry silk attracts a small piece of paper. What happens to the pen and cloth during rubbing?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Resistors R₁ =4 Ω and R₂ =5 Ω are in parallel across the same voltage. Find P₁:P₂.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω supplies two parallel resistors, 12 Ω and 6 Ω. Find the magnitude of current in the 12 Ω resistor.
questions.ai_explanation: The parallel equivalent is 12 ×6/(12 +6) =4 Ω. Including internal resistance gives 5 Ω, so total current is 12/5 =2.4 A. Terminal voltage is 2.4 ×4 =9.6 V, giving 9.6/12 =0.8 A in the 12 Ω resistor.
questions.explanation: The parallel equivalent is 12 ×6/(12 +6) =4 Ω. Including internal resistance gives 5 Ω, so total current is 12/5 =2.4 A. Terminal voltage is 2.4 ×4 =9.6 V, giving 9.6/12 =0.8 A in the 12 Ω resistor.

questions.question: If two parallel conductors carry currents flowing in the same direction, the conductors will

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A sinusoidal alternating voltage has frequency 50 Hz. P is an upward zero crossing and R is the immediately following downward zero crossing. Find the time from P to R.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is the dimension of pressure?

questions.question: A simple pendulum at small amplitude passes its lowest point twice per second. Find its length to two decimal places, using g =10 m/s².
questions.ai_explanation: A pendulum crosses its lowest point twice per complete oscillation, so two crossings per second mean period 1 s. From T =2π√(L/g), L =10/(4π²) =0.253… m, or 0.25 m to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Three non-collinear points are O, A and B. Vector P runs from O to A, Q from O to B, and R from B to A. Which relation is correct?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 20 N load is held at rest by two symmetric cords, each making 30° above horizontal. Find the tension T in each cord.

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics

questions.question: An empty 60 litre tank has mass 10 kg. Find its mass when full of fuel of relative density 0.72. Use water density 1000 kg/m³.

questions.explanation: The fuel volume is 60 L =0.060 m³. Its density is 0.72 ×1000 =720 kg/m³, so fuel mass is 43.2 kg. Adding the 10 kg empty tank gives 53.2 kg.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A mercury thermometer’s thread lengths at 0 °C, 100 °C and an unknown temperature are 25 mm, 225 mm and 175 mm respectively. Assuming linear calibration, find the unknown temperature.
questions.ai_explanation: The 100 °C interval corresponds to 225 −25 =200 mm. A 175 mm reading is 150 mm above zero, so temperature is 150/200 ×100 =75.0 °C.
